prompt: Codes use letters and digits and must contain at least one digit. A developer counts by choosing a digit position, choosing its digit, then freely filling the other positions. What is the flaw?

options.text: It misses all codes with two digits.
options.explanation: Those codes are counted, but more than once.
All-letter codes are exactly the invalid cases.

options.text: A code with several digits is counted once for each possible designated digit.
options.explanation: The selected position is extra information not present in the final code.

options.text: It counts order even though codes are unordered.
options.explanation: Code positions do matter; the problem is multiple representations of the same code.

workedExample: Consider `a1b2c3`. The chosen digit position could be the position of 1, 2 or 3, so the same final code is produced three times. Instead, count all codes and subtract those containing only letters. That complement is disjoint and counts each valid code once.
